newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump, pushed up by SKB bank.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump, pushed up by SKB bank.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their spectacular winning streak on Tuesday, adding on another 3.56 percent on the back of vibrant demand for bank SKB, after its one-week suspension.
Traders said the market needs to consolidate gains after its sharp and rapid rise before pressing on towards higher ground.
"SKB's shares were expected to jump even more, but obviously there was enough demand at prices below 60,000 tolars," Andrej Potocnik, a trader at brokerage BPH said.
Demand for SKB soared due to the bank's plan to list its global depository receipts on the London Stock Exchange by mid- February -- approved by the Bank of Slovenia last week.
The 10-share SBI index jumped 55.81 points to 1,622.7. The index has risen 37 percent since the first trading day of the year.
